questions.question: Which wireless transmission wave has a frequency range of 1 GHz to 300 GHz, is unidirectional and requires line-of-sight propagation?
questions.explanation: Microwaves range from 1 GHz to 300 GHz, are unidirectional, cannot penetrate walls or hills and need line-of-sight, so they are used for radar and satellite links. Radio waves (3 KHz to 1 GHz) are omni-directional.

questions.concept: str.title() capitalises first letter of each word
questions.question: What does the Python string method title() do, as in 'hello WORLD!'.title()?

options.A: Converts the first letter of each word to uppercase
options.B: Converts all lowercase letters to uppercase
options.C: Converts all uppercase letters to lowercase
options.D: Converts only the first letter of the string to uppercase

questions.explanation: title() converts the first letter of each word to uppercase, so 'hello WORLD!'.title() gives 'Hello World!'. upper() and lower() change the case of all letters.

questions.concept: Herman Hollerith designed tabulating machine for punched-card data
questions.question: Which computing device did Herman Hollerith design?

options.D: A tabulating machine for punched-card data

questions.explanation: Herman Hollerith designed a tabulating machine for summarising data stored on punched cards. The Pascaline was by Blaise Pascal, the Analytical Engine by Charles Babbage and the stored program concept by John von Neumann.

questions.question: Cohesion measures the functional strength of a module and coupling measures interdependence between modules. What combination is desired in a good design?
questions.explanation: A good design keeps cohesion strong so each module does one job well, and coupling low so modules depend little on each other.

questions.concept: Binary search iteration count for first element
questions.question: Binary search with mid = (first + last) // 2 is applied to the sorted list [2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 12, 17, 19, 23, 29, 31, 37, 41, 43]. How many iterations are needed to find key = 2?
questions.explanation: The mid indices visited are 7, 3, 1 and then 0, where 2 is found, so it takes 4 iterations. Each unsuccessful comparison halves the search area.

questions.question: Which technique provides a one-time session key for two communicating parties?
questions.explanation: Diffie-Hellman exchanges keys securely and provides a one-time session key for two parties. RSA is a public-key algorithm, while DES and AES are encryption standards.

questions.concept: Hibernate mode for long idle periods
questions.question: In Windows, which power option is meant for a computer that will not be used for a long time?
questions.explanation: Hibernate mode is used when the computer will not be used for a long time, while Sleep mode is for short periods of no use.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes method overloading in Java?

options.A: Same name and same signature in parent and child classes, using dynamic binding
options.B: Same name but different signatures, resolved at runtime by dynamic binding
options.C: Same name but different signatures in one class, using static binding
options.D: Same signature redefined in a subclass, resolved at compile time

questions.explanation: Overloading uses the same method name with different signatures within the same class and is resolved at compile time with static binding. Overriding uses the same signature between parent and child classes with dynamic binding.

questions.question: In a relational database table, the number of columns defines the ____ of the relation.
questions.explanation: The number of columns (attributes) in a table defines the degree of the relation.

questions.concept: Order of four stages of MQTT
questions.question: What is the correct order of the four stages of MQTT?
questions.explanation: The four stages of MQTT are Connection, Authentication, Communication and Termination, in that order.

questions.question: The ASCII value of 'A' is 65, and each lowercase letter is 32 more than its uppercase letter. What is the decimal ASCII value of 'e'?
questions.explanation: 'E' is 65 + 4 = 69, and adding the uppercase-to-lowercase difference of 32 gives 101 for 'e'. This matches 'a' = 97 plus 4.

questions.concept: Operations listed for context-free languages (concatenation, not intersection/complement/difference)
questions.question: According to the operations listed by language class, which operation is listed for Context-Free Languages (Type 2)?
questions.explanation: The operations listed for context-free languages are union, concatenation, Kleene star and Kleene plus. Intersection and complement appear for context-sensitive and regular languages, and difference only for regular languages.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about optical fiber cable are true? (Select all that apply)

options.A: It is not affected by electromagnetic noise
options.B: It is unidirectional, so full-duplex needs two cables
options.C: It is less expensive than twisted pair cable
options.D: It carries data as electrical signals in a copper core

questions.explanation: Optical fiber carries data as light, has high bandwidth and is not affected by electromagnetic noise. It is expensive and unidirectional, so two cables are required for full-duplex communication.

questions.concept: Unordered list type values disc, circle, square
questions.question: Which set gives the valid list type styles for an HTML unordered list?
questions.explanation: The type of an unordered list (<ul>) may be disc, circle or square. Values such as 1, A, a, I and i are numbering styles for ordered lists.

questions.concept: list.insert() shifts later elements then index() returns new position
questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?
lst = [10, 20, 30]
lst.insert(2, 25)
print(lst.index(30))
questions.explanation: insert(2, 25) places 25 at index 2, so the list becomes [10, 20, 25, 30]. index(30) returns the first index of 30, which is now 3.

questions.question: Which statement about the MySQL data types CHAR(n) and VARCHAR(n) is correct?

options.A: CHAR(n) pads shorter values with spaces; VARCHAR(n) uses only needed bytes
options.B: VARCHAR(n) pads shorter values with spaces; CHAR(n) uses only needed bytes
options.C: Both CHAR(n) and VARCHAR(n) allow a maximum length of 255
options.D: CHAR(n) allows lengths up to 65535; VARCHAR(n) only up to 255

questions.explanation: CHAR(n) is fixed-length (0 to 255) and pads remaining spaces. VARCHAR(n) is variable-length (0 to 65535) and uses only the bytes actually needed.

questions.question: Which software process model is suitable only for small programming exercises of about 100-200 lines of code?
questions.explanation: The Build & Fix model suits programming exercises of up to 100-200 LOC and is not suitable for large or complex work.

questions.question: Which IoT protocol is mainly used where real-time data exchange is required, for example in autonomous vehicles, power generation and robotics?
questions.explanation: DDS is used in situations needing real-time data exchange such as autonomous vehicles, power generation and robotics. AMQP uses queues for asynchronous communication, and CoAP targets constrained devices.

questions.question: In asymmetric-key encryption for confidentiality, which key does the receiver use to decrypt the message?
questions.explanation: In asymmetric-key ciphers the sender encrypts with the public key and the receiver decrypts with the private key, which the receiver keeps secret.

questions.question: The elements 12, 29, 45, 72 and 18 are hashed into a table of size 10 using h(element) = element % 10. Which two elements collide?
questions.explanation: 12 % 10 = 2 and 72 % 10 = 2, so both map to index 2 and collide. The others map to 9, 5 and 8.

questions.question: Which pairing of operating system type and example is correct?
questions.explanation: MS-DOS is single-user, single-tasking. Windows Server is multi-user, multi-tasking, and Windows 2000 is listed as a client/server OS.

questions.question: In HTML, which attribute refers to the colour state of a visited link?
questions.explanation: The vlink attribute refers to a visited link. The active link is represented separately from visited links.

questions.question: Which statement about RAM types is correct?

options.A: SRAM uses capacitors and must be refreshed often
options.B: DRAM uses transistors and is used as cache
options.C: SRAM has slower access time than DRAM
options.D: DRAM uses capacitors and must be refreshed often

questions.explanation: DRAM stores bits in capacitors and must be refreshed many times per second. SRAM uses transistors, has faster access and is used for cache memory.

questions.question: Which contribution to the Theory of Computation is credited to Alonzo Church?
questions.explanation: Alonzo Church developed lambda calculus and contributed to the Church-Turing thesis. The Turing machine was invented by Alan Turing.

questions.question: Before it was named Java, the Java programming language was called:
questions.explanation: Before Java, the language's name was Oak.
